How DeFi Yields Work

Where Does DeFi Yield Come From?

DeFi yields aren't magic — they're earned from real economic activity. Understanding the source helps you assess sustainability and risk.

📊
Trading Fees
AMMs like Curve and Uniswap collect fees from every trade. LPs earn a share of these fees proportional to their liquidity.
Example: Curve 3pool ~3–8% APY from fees alone
🏦
Lending Interest
Protocols like Aave and Compound let users borrow assets, paying interest to lenders. Supply rates fluctuate with demand.
Example: Aave USDC supply ~2–5% APY variable rate
⛓️
Staking Rewards
Proof-of-stake networks reward validators for securing the chain. Liquid staking (Lido, Rocket Pool) lets anyone participate.
Example: Ethereum staking (Lido) ~3–5% APY via liquid staking
🚀
Token Incentives
Protocols bootstrap liquidity by distributing governance tokens. These inflation rewards boost APY but dilute over time.
Example: New protocol launch 20–100%+ APY (token-heavy)
💱
Liquidity Mining
Protocols pay liquidity providers with native tokens to bootstrap markets. The token value can be volatile — YMMV.
Example: Balancer LP rewards ~5–15% APY in BAL tokens
📐
Real Yield / Fee Revenue
Some protocols distribute real revenue (not inflation) to stakers. This is considered "sustainable" yield — though crypto is rarely simple.
Example: GMX GLP rewards ~8–20% APY from fees + esGMX

FAQ

Frequently Asked Questions

APY (Annual Percentage Yield) in DeFi is the effective annual return on your crypto investment, accounting for the effect of compounding interest. Unlike simple APR, APY includes reinvested earnings, so your gains generate their own gains over time. The more frequently your interest is compounded, the higher your effective APY will be relative to the stated APR.
APY is calculated using the formula: APY = (1 + r/n)n - 1, where r is the annual interest rate (as a decimal) and n is the number of compounding periods per year. For example, 10% APR compounded monthly gives APY = (1 + 0.10/12)12 - 1 ≈ 10.47%. For continuous compounding, APY = er - 1.
APR (Annual Percentage Rate) is the simple annual interest rate without compounding. It tells you how much interest you earn on the original principal only. APY includes the effect of compounding, showing the true yearly return when interest is reinvested. For example, 10% APR with monthly compounding equals approximately 10.47% APY. The gap widens dramatically at higher rates — at 100% APR, monthly compounding yields ~170% APY.
Generally, more frequent compounding yields higher returns — theoretically, continuous compounding is optimal. However, practical factors matter: on-chain transactions have gas fees that can exceed the benefit of compounding small amounts daily. For large positions, daily or continuous compounding is best. For smaller positions, weekly or monthly may be more practical. Consider gas costs relative to your position size before compounding aggressively.
DeFi yields are influenced by: (1) Trading volume — more volume means more fees for AMM LPs. (2) Supply and demand for capital — when borrowing demand is high, lenders earn more. (3) Token incentives — protocols often subsidize yields with token emissions. (4) Market conditions — volatile markets tend to generate higher trading fees. (5) Protocol risk — higher risk protocols offer higher yields to compensate. Yields typically fluctuate daily based on these factors.
